author.name: William Shakespeare
author.biography: Shakespeare left Stratford-upon-Avon for a career in London's theatres, where he worked as an actor, playwright and company shareholder. He knew stories as things people performed before other people, with attention, sympathy and judgment changing from moment to moment. Shakespeare made the public stage a place where an audience could hear a mind arguing with itself. Hamlet turns that theatrical intimacy into a test of action under uncertainty.

hook.text: How can you act when you no longer know whom to trust?

paragraphs: Hamlet's father is dead. His mother has married his uncle. The court wants the young prince to accept the new arrangement and carry on. Then a claim about the past makes acceptance seem impossible.

Shakespeare gives us the uncomfortable company of a mind that can find an objection to almost any course of action. Doubt can protect Hamlet from being used. It can also become a way of delaying the moment when a choice must have consequences. Around him, other people are watching, guessing and trying to control what can be known.

The play is funny, cruel and unexpectedly intimate. Listen for what changes when a speech has an audience and when a character seems alone. If you suspected that the world around you was built on a lie, what evidence would be enough to make you act?

orientation.text: Hamlet is the prince of Denmark. Soliloquies give access to his thinking, but his performances before other characters may have very different purposes.
